subject: history
topic: Leaded petrol lowered the IQ of a generation
angle: Lead exposure in children is linked to measurable IQ point losses, structural brain changes in adults, and significant economic costs in Mexico.
title: The Structural Cost of Lead

hooks.text: How much of your behavior is a chemical reflex?
You assume your brain is fixed. Evidence shows it can be structurally altered.
You are living in a world shaped by old industrial waste.

reveal.headline: Lead exposure is linked to structural changes in the adult brain.
reveal.body: Research shows childhood lead exposure is associated with region-specific reductions in adult gray matter volume in the prefrontal cortex and the anterior cingulate cortex.

explain.headline: The biological impact of lead exposure.
explain.body: Exposure is linked to cognitive impairment, alterations in executive function, abnormal social behavior, and perturbations in fine motor control. It affects the physical structure of the brain.

matters.headline: The invisible cost of history.
matters.body: That may be why some communities experience persistent cognitive challenges. These structural changes remain in the brain long after the initial exposure occurs.

example.headline: A child playing in a city park.
example.body: Dust settles on the grass. It stays in the soil. It enters the body through the air and the ground during a routine afternoon of play.

verdict: The evidence shows that lead exposure is associated with measurable cognitive deficits, structural brain volume reductions, and substantial economic impacts.
caveat: The study showing specific IQ point losses in Mexico is an observational study, which shows an association rather than a proven cause.
caption:
Lead exposure leaves permanent marks on human biology. 

Observational studies in Mexico show an association between lead exposure and an average loss of 4.14 IQ points in children. These findings indicate a link rather than a proven cause. 

How does knowing this change how you view your environment?
